newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Bank of Portugal springs rate cut surprise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bank of Portugal springs rate cut surprise.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal surprised markets on Friday, cutting its repurchase pact rate, a key money market indicator, by 30 basis points to 6.0 percent at least a week earlier than expected.

And the Bank signalled that further cuts could be in the offing by lowering its absorption, or drain rate -- the rate at which it offers to soak up excess market funds -- by 10 basis points to 5.7 percent, analysts said.

The traditionally highly cautious central bank, which occasionally wrongfoots analysts with pre-emptive moves, had been expected to wait until after April inflation figures were released next week and, possibly, for the Bank of Spain to move.

Seven out of eight analysts polled by Reuters on Thursday had not expected any reduction in the repo rate this week, and the one that did saw a cut of only 20 basis points. None had foreseen a lowering in the drain rate.

"The Bank is probably anticipating the April inflation figure which is expected to be good and expectations that the Bank of Spain will cut rates next Friday," said Isabel Cabral of Lisbon brokers Fincor.
Official figures, which must be issued by May 15, are expected to show that year-on-year inflation last month fell to a new 30-year low below two percent. The rate stood at 2.5 percent in March.
Despite the fact the rate cut had not been forecast, financial markets showed little reaction to the move with the escudo remaining rock steady against the German mark.
The bond and stock markets also shrugged off the change, although yields on the shorter-term bonds did fall slightly.
Traders said that although the timing was a surprise, a cut had long been forecast and market prices were already discounting an easing in monetary policy.

Some analysts said that the Bank might have decided to act early because of the threat of exchange rate turbulence in the run-up to the next U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting, set for May 20, and the French elections.
Markets are already slightly jittery about whether the Fed will raise rates.

"The stance of the Bank seems intelligent to me, and correct, given the approach of the French elections and some exchange turbulence that could come next week," said Jorge Ferraz of research group Informacao Mercados Financeiros.
Despite more robust Portuguese economic growth than initially expected, analysts said that there would still be room for further cuts in interest rates later in the year.

One analyst said that the Bank had even left the door open for a further cut in its drain rate, the most important official money market rate, if the Bank of Spain eases, as it is widely expected to do, after April inflation figures are released next week.

"I believe the 5.70 percent drain rate is high and if Spain cuts the repo 25 basis points on Friday, to 5.25 percent, the Bank of Portugal could cut again to 5.50 percent," said Federico Alegria of Banco Essi.
